concepts.en: How can we care for our environment?

summary.big_en: A habitat is the place where a living thing lives.

glossary.def: Look for what is the same and what is different.
glossary.example: Compare two habitats near your school (p.5).
glossary.example_vi: Hãy so sánh hai nơi sống gần trường em.

glossary.def: The place where a living thing lives.
glossary.example: A wall can be a habitat for a small plant (p.3).
glossary.example_vi: Một bức tường có thể là nơi sống của cây nhỏ.

glossary.def: A word you write on a drawing to name a part.
glossary.example: Label your drawing to say what each thing is (p.4).
glossary.example_vi: Hãy ghi tên từng thứ trên hình em vẽ.

glossary.def: A small copy of a real thing.
glossary.example: Make a model of a habitat for fish in a box (p.5).
glossary.example_vi: Hãy làm mô hình nơi sống của cá trong một cái hộp.

glossary.def: The air, water and land around us.
glossary.example: People, animals and plants all live in the environment (p.2).
glossary.example_vi: Người, động vật và cây cối đều sống trong môi trường.

glossary.def: The place where a living thing stays.
glossary.example: The wall is the plant's home (p.3).
glossary.example_vi: Bức tường là nhà của cây đó.

glossary.def: Near the place where you live.
glossary.example: Your local environment has many habitats (p.4).
glossary.example_vi: Môi trường quanh nhà em có nhiều nơi sống khác nhau.

points.t: A habitat gives a living thing everything it needs to live (p.3).
A habitat can be very small, like a wall, or very large, like a forest (p.3).
Plants cannot move from place to place, but animals can move in their habitat (p.4).

glossary.def: A thin line where something is split open.
glossary.example: Roots grow down a crack to find soil (p.8).
glossary.example_vi: Rễ cây chui xuống khe nứt để tìm đất.

glossary.def: Say what something is like.
glossary.example: Describe the place a plant lives (p.7).
glossary.example_vi: Hãy tả nơi mà cây đó sống.

glossary.def: A place that is very hot and very dry.
glossary.example: A cactus can live in a hot desert (p.11).
glossary.example_vi: Cây xương rồng sống được ở sa mạc nóng.

glossary.def: A picture you take with a camera.
glossary.example: Take a photograph of your plant (p.8).
glossary.example_vi: Hãy chụp ảnh cái cây của em.

glossary.def: Act as if you are someone or something else.
glossary.example: Pretend you are one of the three plants (p.10).
glossary.example_vi: Hãy giả vờ em là một trong ba cái cây.

glossary.def: Write or draw what you see.
glossary.example: Record your plants and their habitats in a table (p.8).
glossary.example_vi: Hãy ghi lại cây và nơi sống của chúng vào bảng.

points.t: All plants need water, and many plants grow in or by water (p.7).
Rice needs a warm habitat with a lot of light and water (p.10).
A cactus needs a very hot habitat with light and very little water (p.11).
Pond weed needs a habitat underwater, and it must not get very cold (p.11).

summary.big_en: Animals often hide, so we look for clues to find them.

glossary.def: Make something want to come.
glossary.example: More insects may attract other animals (p.17).
glossary.example_vi: Nhiều côn trùng có thể thu hút những con vật khác tới.

glossary.def: Small signs that show an animal was here.
glossary.example: Tracks and droppings are clues (p.14).
glossary.example_vi: Dấu chân và phân là những dấu vết.

glossary.def: The waste an animal leaves behind.
glossary.example: Droppings tell us that an animal is near (p.14).
glossary.example_vi: Phân cho ta biết có con vật ở gần.

glossary.def: Something an animal lays, with a baby inside.
glossary.example: Insects lay eggs in the sticks (p.17).
glossary.example_vi: Côn trùng đẻ trứng trong đám que.

glossary.def: Go somewhere you cannot be seen.
glossary.example: Snails like to hide in cool damp places (p.16).
glossary.example_vi: Ốc sên thích trốn ở chỗ mát và ẩm.

glossary.def: A very small animal, like a beetle or an ant.
glossary.example: An insect hotel is a habitat for insects (p.17).
glossary.example_vi: Khách sạn côn trùng là nơi sống cho côn trùng.

glossary.def: Make an animal afraid so it runs away.
glossary.example: Be quiet so that you don't scare the animals (p.15).
glossary.example_vi: Hãy im lặng để không làm con vật sợ.

glossary.def: Marks that an animal's feet leave on the ground.
glossary.example: We can see tracks in soft soil (p.14).
glossary.example_vi: Ta thấy dấu chân trên đất mềm.

points.t: Animals hide from us, so they are harder to observe than plants (p.15).
Clues that an animal lives here are tracks, droppings, eaten leaves and birds singing (p.14).
Small animals need a safe place to live close to food (p.17).

summary.big_en: We dig up rocks to build things, but digging damages the environment.

glossary.def: Take water in.
glossary.example: Chalk absorbs water (p.23).
glossary.example_vi: Đá phấn hút nước.

glossary.def: Something that breaks rock into pieces with a bang.
glossary.example: Sometimes we use explosives to break rock (p.24).
glossary.example_vi: Đôi khi người ta dùng thuốc nổ để phá đá.

glossary.def: Small stones from a river bed.
glossary.example: From rivers we dig sand, gravel and pebbles (p.25).
glossary.example_vi: Từ sông ta đào cát, sỏi và đá cuội.

glossary.def: A place where we dig rock deep underground.
glossary.example: We get coal and salt from a deep mine (p.24).
glossary.example_vi: Ta lấy than và muối từ mỏ sâu.

glossary.def: A place where we dig rock at the surface.
glossary.example: We get limestone and slate from a quarry (p.24).
glossary.example_vi: Ta lấy đá vôi và đá phiến từ mỏ lộ thiên.

glossary.def: A small piece you take to look at.
glossary.example: Sofia and Zara have a sample of rock (p.22).
glossary.example_vi: Sofia và Zara có một mẩu đá.

glossary.def: Another name for small rocks.
glossary.example: Stones is another name for small rocks (p.25).
glossary.example_vi: Đá nhỏ còn được gọi là sỏi đá.

glossary.def: Move water round and round.
glossary.example: Add water and swirl the water (p.26).
glossary.example_vi: Đổ nước vào rồi khuấy cho nước xoay.

glossary.def: Water cannot go in.
glossary.example: Slate is waterproof, so we use it for roofs (p.21).
glossary.example_vi: Đá phiến không thấm nước nên được dùng lợp mái.

points.t: Planet Earth is made of rocks (p.20).
Rocks can be strong, soft or waterproof, and we choose a rock for the job (p.21).
Most rocks do not burn, but coal is a rock that burns (p.21).
When people dig up rocks, plants and animals lose their homes (p.25).

summary.big_en: We can care for the environment by picking up litter and recycling.

glossary.def: Rubbish left in the wrong place.
glossary.example: This beach is covered in litter (p.28).
glossary.example_vi: Bãi biển này đầy rác.

glossary.def: What a thing is made of.
glossary.example: The arrows tell us that the material can be used again (p.30).
glossary.example_vi: Mũi tên cho biết vật liệu đó dùng lại được.

glossary.def: A place kept safe for plants and animals.
glossary.example: The children want to make the garden into a nature reserve (p.30).
glossary.example_vi: Các bạn nhỏ muốn biến khu vườn thành khu bảo tồn.

glossary.def: Dirty air, water or land.
glossary.example: Pollution is bad for animals and plants (p.28).
glossary.example_vi: Ô nhiễm có hại cho động vật và cây cối.

glossary.def: Keep something safe.
glossary.example: We can protect the animals and plants on the beach (p.28).
glossary.example_vi: Ta có thể bảo vệ động vật và cây cối trên bãi biển.

glossary.def: Use a material again instead of throwing it away.
glossary.example: We can recycle glass, paper, plastic, card and metal (p.30).
glossary.example_vi: Ta có thể tái chế thuỷ tinh, giấy, nhựa, bìa và kim loại.

points.t: Pollution harms the animals and plants that live near it (p.28).
The recycling sign has arrows that mean the material can be used again (p.30).
A nature reserve makes a better habitat for plants and animals (p.30).
Litter can be dangerous, so talk to an adult before you pick it up (p.31).

summary.big_en: A push or a pull is a force, and forces make things start moving and stop moving.

glossary.def: A push or a pull.
glossary.example: Pushes and pulls are forces (p.37).
glossary.example_vi: Lực đẩy và lực kéo đều là lực.

glossary.def: A force that moves something away from you.
glossary.example: This girl is pushing the box away from her (p.37).
glossary.example_vi: Bạn nữ này đang đẩy cái hộp ra xa mình.

glossary.def: A force that moves something towards you.
glossary.example: These boys are pulling the rope towards them (p.37).
glossary.example_vi: Các bạn nam này đang kéo dây về phía mình.

glossary.def: In the other direction, further from you.
glossary.example: A push is a force away from you (p.37).
glossary.example_vi: Lực đẩy là lực hướng ra xa mình.

glossary.def: In the direction of something, closer to you.
glossary.example: A pull is a force towards you (p.37).
glossary.example_vi: Lực kéo là lực hướng về phía mình.

glossary.def: To pull something so it gets longer.
glossary.example: Omar pulls his toys with elastic that can stretch (p.39).
glossary.example_vi: Omar kéo đồ chơi bằng dây chun co giãn được.

glossary.def: To press something so it changes shape.
glossary.example: Zara launches her rocket by squashing the bottle (p.40).
glossary.example_vi: Zara phóng tên lửa bằng cách bóp chai.

glossary.def: To send something up into the air.
glossary.example: Use a small push to launch your rocket (p.40).
glossary.example_vi: Dùng lực đẩy nhỏ để phóng tên lửa.

glossary.def: A tube that shoots up into the air.
glossary.example: Zara has made a paper rocket (p.40).
glossary.example_vi: Zara đã làm một chiếc tên lửa giấy.

points.t: Pushes and pulls are forces (p.37).
A push is a force away from you (p.37). The girl pushes the box so it moves further from her.
A pull is a force towards you (p.37). The boys pull the rope so it comes closer to them.
Forces can make things move and forces can make things stop (p.37). The man uses a push to stop the ball.
There are small forces and big forces (p.39). A heavier toy needs a bigger pull to make it move.

experiments.title: Using forces to move things and stop things
experiments.summary: Push and then pull a ball, and try the same with a balloon, a chair and a pencil. Then find a way to make each one stop.
experiments.result: A push or a pull starts each object moving, and another force is needed to stop it.

experiments.title: Make a paper rocket launcher
experiments.summary: Squash a plastic bottle with a push to launch a paper rocket. Predict how high it will go with a small push, then with a big push.
experiments.result: The bigger the push, the higher the rocket goes.

checklists.title: I can do this

items.sign: Say how a push or pull

items.look_for: and say if they are correct

checklists.note: The section's own Look what I can do! list (p.41).

summary.big_en: Forces can change the shape of some objects, and results often follow a pattern.

glossary.def: The form of an object — how it looks on the outside.
glossary.example: We can use forces to change the shape of wood (p.43).
glossary.example_vi: Ta có thể dùng lực để làm thay đổi hình dạng của gỗ.

glossary.def: A thing you can see and touch.
glossary.example: Look at these objects and see how their shape changes (p.43).
glossary.example_vi: Hãy nhìn các vật này và xem hình dạng của chúng đổi thế nào.

glossary.def: To find out how big, how long or how heavy something is.
glossary.example: Count the bricks to measure the height (p.43).
glossary.example_vi: Đếm số viên gạch để đo chiều cao.

glossary.def: How high something is from the ground.
glossary.example: Drop the ball again from a different height (p.43).
glossary.example_vi: Thả quả bóng lại từ một độ cao khác.

glossary.def: To try something out carefully to find an answer.
glossary.example: Investigate what happens when there is a bigger pull (p.45).
glossary.example_vi: Hãy thử nghiệm xem chuyện gì xảy ra khi kéo mạnh hơn.

glossary.def: What you find out when you try something.
glossary.example: Record your results in a table (p.44).
glossary.example_vi: Ghi kết quả của em vào bảng.

glossary.def: A similar change in the result each time.
glossary.example: Try to find the pattern in your results (p.45).
glossary.example_vi: Hãy tìm quy luật trong kết quả của em.

points.t: Forces can change the shape of some objects (p.42).
We use forces to make bread, to press clay into a pot and to change the shape of wood (p.43).
A pattern in results is when there is a similar change in the result each time (p.44).
Adding one book each time makes the measurements fair, because only one thing changes (p.46).

experiments.title: Finding patterns in results
experiments.summary: Drop a ball of soft clay, measuring the drop height by counting bricks. Roll it back into a ball and drop it again from a different height.
experiments.result: The higher the drop, the flatter the clay ball becomes.

experiments.title: How forces can change rubber bands
experiments.summary: Hang books from a rubber band, adding one book at a time, and measure how long the band becomes using sticky notes.
experiments.result: Each extra book pulls harder, so the rubber band stretches a little longer each time.

checklists.title: I can do this

items.look_for: change the shape of some objects

checklists.note: The section's own Look what I can do! list (p.46).

watch_out.wrong: There is no pattern in my results.
watch_out.right: Lola's results do have a pattern — she did not add the books one at a time, so the pattern was hard to see (p.45-46).

summary.big_en: A force is what makes something speed up or slow down.

glossary.def: How fast something is moving.
glossary.example: Your speed is how fast you are moving (p.47).
glossary.example_vi: Tốc độ là mức độ nhanh chậm khi em di chuyển.

glossary.def: To start going faster.
glossary.example: Going faster is called speeding up (p.47).
glossary.example_vi: Đi nhanh hơn thì gọi là tăng tốc.

glossary.def: To start going slower.
glossary.example: Going slower is called slowing down (p.47).
glossary.example_vi: Đi chậm lại thì gọi là giảm tốc.

glossary.def: The parts of a bike you push with your feet.
glossary.example: To go faster on a bike you push on the pedals (p.47).
glossary.example_vi: Muốn đạp xe nhanh hơn thì em đạp mạnh vào bàn đạp.

glossary.def: The parts that make a bike or a car slow down.
glossary.example: To go slower you pull on the brakes (p.47).
glossary.example_vi: Muốn đi chậm lại thì em bóp phanh.

glossary.def: To say why something happens.
glossary.example: Try to help Sofia explain the pattern (p.50).
glossary.example_vi: Hãy giúp Sofia giải thích quy luật đó.

points.t: Your speed is how fast you are moving (p.47).
Going faster is called speeding up, and going slower is called slowing down (p.47).
When something speeds up or slows down it is because of a force (p.47).
On a bike you push the pedals to speed up and pull the brakes to slow down (p.47).
Air can push a moving ball and make it slow down (p.49).

experiments.title: Blow the ball
experiments.summary: One child pushes a ball towards another, who blows towards it. Then try blowing from behind the ball instead.
experiments.result: Blowing towards the ball slows it down, and blowing behind it speeds it up, without touching it.

checklists.title: I can do this

items.look_for: make something move faster or slower
about making things speed up or slow down

checklists.note: The section's own Look what I can do! list (p.51).

summary.big_en: A force is also needed to make something change direction.

glossary.def: The way something is going.
glossary.example: When you turn to go a different way you change direction (p.53).
glossary.example_vi: Khi em quay sang đường khác là em đổi hướng.

glossary.def: To move so you face a different way.
glossary.example: This boat pushed the water to make it turn (p.53).
glossary.example_vi: Chiếc thuyền này đẩy nước để quay hướng.

glossary.def: A drawing that shows only the important things, with labels and arrows.
glossary.example: A diagram is different from a picture (p.54).
glossary.example_vi: Sơ đồ khác với bức tranh.

points.t: When you are going one way and then turn to go a different way, you change direction (p.53).
Forces are needed to make things change direction (p.53). The boat pushes the water to turn.
A diagram shows only the important things, with labels and arrows, so it is different from a picture (p.54).

experiments.title: This way or that way?
experiments.summary: Draw a diagram predicting which way a ball will go when it is pushed, then push the ball and draw the real result in another colour.
experiments.result: The push changes the ball's direction, and the two colours show at a glance whether the prediction was right.

checklists.title: I can do this

items.look_for: if my predictions are correct or not

checklists.note: The section's own Look what I can do! list (p.55).

flashcards.example_en: Take a photograph of your plant (p.8).
flashcards.example_vi: Hãy chụp ảnh cái cây của em.

flashcards.back_en: Act as if you are someone or something else.
flashcards.example_en: Pretend you are one of the three plants (p.10).
flashcards.example_vi: Hãy giả vờ em là một trong ba cái cây.

flashcards.back_en: The waste an animal leaves behind.
flashcards.example_en: Droppings tell us that an animal is near (p.14).
flashcards.example_vi: Phân cho ta biết có con vật ở gần.

flashcards.back_en: Something an animal lays, with a baby inside.
flashcards.example_en: Insects lay eggs in the sticks (p.17).
flashcards.example_vi: Côn trùng đẻ trứng trong đám que.

flashcards.back_en: Make an animal afraid so it runs away.
flashcards.example_en: Be quiet so that you don't scare the animals (p.15).
flashcards.example_vi: Hãy im lặng để không làm con vật sợ.

flashcards.back_en: Something that breaks rock into pieces with a bang.
flashcards.example_en: Sometimes we use explosives to break rock (p.24).
flashcards.example_vi: Đôi khi người ta dùng thuốc nổ để phá đá.

flashcards.back_en: A small piece you take to look at.
flashcards.example_en: Sofia and Zara have a sample of rock (p.22).
flashcards.example_vi: Sofia và Zara có một mẩu đá.

flashcards.back_en: Another name for small rocks.
flashcards.example_en: Stones is another name for small rocks (p.25).
flashcards.example_vi: Đá nhỏ còn được gọi là sỏi đá.

flashcards.back_en: Move water round and round.
flashcards.example_en: Add water and swirl the water (p.26).
flashcards.example_vi: Đổ nước vào rồi khuấy cho nước xoay.

flashcards.back_en: What a thing is made of.
flashcards.example_en: The arrows tell us that the material can be used again (p.30).
flashcards.example_vi: Mũi tên cho biết vật liệu đó dùng lại được.

flashcards.back_en: A push or a pull.
flashcards.example_en: Pushes and pulls are forces (p.37).
flashcards.example_vi: Lực đẩy và lực kéo đều là lực.

flashcards.back_en: A force that moves something away from you.
flashcards.example_en: This girl is pushing the box away from her (p.37).
flashcards.example_vi: Bạn nữ này đang đẩy cái hộp ra xa mình.

flashcards.back_en: A force that moves something towards you.
flashcards.example_en: These boys are pulling the rope towards them (p.37).
flashcards.example_vi: Các bạn nam này đang kéo dây về phía mình.

flashcards.back_en: In the other direction, further from you.
flashcards.example_en: A push is a force away from you (p.37).
flashcards.example_vi: Lực đẩy là lực hướng ra xa mình.

flashcards.back_en: In the direction of something, closer to you.
flashcards.example_en: A pull is a force towards you (p.37).
flashcards.example_vi: Lực kéo là lực hướng về phía mình.

flashcards.back_en: To pull something so it gets longer.
flashcards.example_en: Omar pulls his toys with elastic that can stretch (p.39).
flashcards.example_vi: Omar kéo đồ chơi bằng dây chun co giãn được.

flashcards.back_en: To press something so it changes shape.
flashcards.example_en: Zara launches her rocket by squashing the bottle (p.40).
flashcards.example_vi: Zara phóng tên lửa bằng cách bóp chai.

flashcards.back_en: To send something up into the air.
flashcards.example_en: Use a small push to launch your rocket (p.40).
flashcards.example_vi: Dùng lực đẩy nhỏ để phóng tên lửa.

flashcards.back_en: A tube that shoots up into the air.
flashcards.example_en: Zara has made a paper rocket (p.40).
flashcards.example_vi: Zara đã làm một chiếc tên lửa giấy.

flashcards.back_en: The form of an object — how it looks on the outside.
flashcards.example_en: We can use forces to change the shape of wood (p.43).
flashcards.example_vi: Ta có thể dùng lực để làm thay đổi hình dạng của gỗ.

flashcards.back_en: A thing you can see and touch.
flashcards.example_en: Look at these objects and see how their shape changes (p.43).
flashcards.example_vi: Hãy nhìn các vật này và xem hình dạng của chúng đổi thế nào.

flashcards.back_en: To find out how big, how long or how heavy something is.
flashcards.example_en: Count the bricks to measure the height (p.43).
flashcards.example_vi: Đếm số viên gạch để đo chiều cao.

flashcards.back_en: How high something is from the ground.
flashcards.example_en: Drop the ball again from a different height (p.43).
flashcards.example_vi: Thả quả bóng lại từ một độ cao khác.

flashcards.back_en: To try something out carefully to find an answer.
flashcards.example_en: Investigate what happens when there is a bigger pull (p.45).
flashcards.example_vi: Hãy thử nghiệm xem chuyện gì xảy ra khi kéo mạnh hơn.

flashcards.back_en: What you find out when you try something.
flashcards.example_en: Record your results in a table (p.44).
flashcards.example_vi: Ghi kết quả của em vào bảng.

flashcards.back_en: A similar change in the result each time.
flashcards.example_en: Try to find the pattern in your results (p.45).
flashcards.example_vi: Hãy tìm quy luật trong kết quả của em.

flashcards.back_en: How fast something is moving.
flashcards.example_en: Your speed is how fast you are moving (p.47).
flashcards.example_vi: Tốc độ là mức độ nhanh chậm khi em di chuyển.

flashcards.back_en: To start going faster.
flashcards.example_en: Going faster is called speeding up (p.47).
flashcards.example_vi: Đi nhanh hơn thì gọi là tăng tốc.

flashcards.back_en: To start going slower.
flashcards.example_en: Going slower is called slowing down (p.47).
flashcards.example_vi: Đi chậm lại thì gọi là giảm tốc.

flashcards.back_en: The parts of a bike you push with your feet.
flashcards.example_en: To go faster on a bike you push on the pedals (p.47).
flashcards.example_vi: Muốn đạp xe nhanh hơn thì em đạp mạnh vào bàn đạp.

flashcards.back_en: The parts that make a bike or a car slow down.
flashcards.example_en: To go slower you pull on the brakes (p.47).
flashcards.example_vi: Muốn đi chậm lại thì em bóp phanh.

flashcards.back_en: To say why something happens.
flashcards.example_en: Try to help Sofia explain the pattern (p.50).
flashcards.example_vi: Hãy giúp Sofia giải thích quy luật đó.

flashcards.back_en: The way something is going.
flashcards.example_en: When you turn to go a different way you change direction (p.53).
flashcards.example_vi: Khi em quay sang đường khác là em đổi hướng.

flashcards.back_en: To move so you face a different way.
flashcards.example_en: This boat pushed the water to make it turn (p.53).
flashcards.example_vi: Chiếc thuyền này đẩy nước để quay hướng.

flashcards.back_en: A drawing that shows only the important things, with labels and arrows.
flashcards.example_en: A diagram is different from a picture (p.54).
flashcards.example_vi: Sơ đồ khác với bức tranh.

quiz.stem_en: What is a habitat?

choices.en: The place a living thing lives

quiz.why_en: A habitat is the place where a living thing lives (p.3).

quiz.stem_en: What does a habitat give a living thing?
quiz.why_en: A habitat gives the living thing everything it needs to live (p.3).

quiz.stem_en: Which one can move around its habitat?
quiz.why_en: Animals can move in their habitat, but plants cannot (p.4).

quiz.stem_en: Is the eagle's habitat large or small?
quiz.why_en: The eagle's habitat is around forests and lakes, so it is very large (p.3).

quiz.stem_en: What does every plant need?
quiz.why_en: All plants need water (p.7).

quiz.stem_en: Where does a cactus live?
quiz.why_en: A cactus needs a habitat which is very hot and needs very little water (p.11).

quiz.stem_en: What does rice need a lot of?
quiz.why_en: Rice needs a habitat which is warm, with lots of light and water (p.10).

quiz.stem_en: Where does pond weed live?
quiz.why_en: Pond weed needs a habitat underwater in a pond, lake or river (p.11).

quiz.stem_en: Why are animals harder to observe than plants?
quiz.why_en: Animals may hide from us, so they are harder to observe (p.15).

quiz.stem_en: Which one is a clue that an animal was here?
quiz.why_en: Tracks, droppings and eaten leaves are clues (p.14).

quiz.stem_en: Where do snails like to hide?
quiz.why_en: Snails like to hide in cool damp places (p.16).

quiz.stem_en: What is an insect hotel made from?
quiz.why_en: The insect hotel is made from sticks and stems (p.17).

quiz.stem_en: What is planet Earth made of?
quiz.why_en: Planet Earth is made of rocks (p.20).

quiz.stem_en: Why do we use slate for roofs?
quiz.why_en: Slate is waterproof (p.21).

quiz.stem_en: Which rock burns?
quiz.why_en: Most rocks do not burn, but coal is a rock that burns (p.21).

quiz.stem_en: Where do we dig rock deep underground?
quiz.why_en: A deep mine is a place where we dig up rock deep underground (p.24).

quiz.stem_en: What happens when people dig up rocks?
quiz.why_en: When people dig up rocks they damage the environment: plants and animals lose their homes (p.25).

quiz.stem_en: What is litter?

choices.en: Rubbish left in the wrong place

quiz.why_en: Litter is rubbish left where it should not be (p.28).

quiz.stem_en: Which of these can we recycle?
quiz.why_en: We can recycle glass, paper, plastic, card, metal and electrical cells (p.30).

quiz.stem_en: What do the arrows on the recycling sign mean?

choices.en: The material can be used again

quiz.why_en: The arrows tell us that the material can be used again (p.30).

quiz.stem_en: What should you do before you pick up litter?
quiz.why_en: Litter can be dangerous, so talk to an adult before you pick up litter (p.31).

quiz.stem_en: What do we call a push or a pull?
quiz.why_en: A push or a pull is a force (p.37).

quiz.stem_en: A girl moves a box so it goes further away from her. What is she using?
quiz.why_en: A push is a force away from you (p.37).

quiz.stem_en: Two boys move a rope so it comes closer to them. What is that force called?
quiz.why_en: A pull is a force towards you (p.37).

quiz.stem_en: A man puts out his hands and a rolling ball stops. What did the force do?
quiz.why_en: Forces can make things move and they can make things stop (p.37).

quiz.stem_en: Which sentence about forces is true?

choices.en: Forces can only make things start moving
Forces can make things move and also make things stop

quiz.why_en: Forces do both jobs (p.37).

quiz.stem_en: One toy is heavy and one toy is light. Which needs the bigger pull to start moving?

choices.en: They need exactly the same pull

quiz.why_en: There are small forces and big forces; a heavier toy needs a bigger pull (p.39).

quiz.stem_en: A paper rocket is launched by squashing a bottle. What happens when the push is bigger?
quiz.why_en: The bigger the push, the higher the rocket goes (p.40).

quiz.stem_en: Omar pulls his toy with a piece of elastic and the elastic gets longer. What is the elastic doing?
quiz.why_en: To stretch is to be pulled so it gets longer (p.39).

quiz.stem_en: What can a force do to a soft object?
quiz.why_en: Forces can change the shape of some objects (p.42).

quiz.stem_en: A baker presses and folds dough to make bread. What is the baker using?
quiz.why_en: We can use forces to make bread (p.43).

quiz.stem_en: You count bricks to find out how high you are holding a clay ball. What are you doing?
quiz.why_en: Count the bricks to measure the height you drop the ball from (p.43).

quiz.stem_en: A clay ball is dropped from higher and higher. What happens to its shape?
quiz.why_en: The higher the drop, the flatter the clay ball becomes (p.43).

quiz.stem_en: What is a pattern in results?

choices.en: A drawing on the front of the book
A result you did not expect
A similar change in the result each time

quiz.why_en: A pattern in results is when there is a similar change in the result each time (p.44).

quiz.stem_en: Books are hung on a rubber band, one more book each time. What happens to the band?

choices.en: It stretches a little longer each time
It stays exactly the same length

quiz.why_en: A bigger pull stretches the rubber band more (p.45).

quiz.stem_en: What does the word speed mean?
quiz.why_en: Your speed is how fast you are moving (p.47).

quiz.stem_en: What is it called when something starts going faster?
quiz.why_en: Going faster is called speeding up (p.47).

quiz.stem_en: On a bike, what do you do to go faster?
quiz.why_en: To go faster on a bike you push on the pedals (p.47).

quiz.stem_en: On a bike, what do you do to go slower?
quiz.why_en: To go slower you pull on the brakes (p.47).

quiz.stem_en: Why does something speed up or slow down?

choices.en: Because of the time of day

quiz.why_en: When something speeds up or slows down it is because of a force (p.47).

quiz.stem_en: A ball rolls along and a child blows towards it. What happens to the ball?
quiz.why_en: The air pushes the ball to make it go slower (p.49).

quiz.stem_en: How can you make a rolling ball go faster without touching it?

choices.en: Blow at it from the front

quiz.why_en: Air pushing from behind speeds the ball up (p.50).

quiz.stem_en: A bowling ball must knock over the pins. What does it need?
quiz.why_en: A bowling ball needs to have lots of speed to knock over the pins (p.51).

quiz.stem_en: What does it mean to change direction?

choices.en: To turn and go a different way

quiz.why_en: When you turn to go a different way you change direction (p.53).

quiz.stem_en: What is needed to make something change direction?
quiz.why_en: Forces are needed to make things change direction (p.53).

quiz.stem_en: A boat turns on the water. How does it do that?
quiz.why_en: This boat has pushed the water to make it turn (p.53).

quiz.stem_en: How is a diagram different from a picture?

choices.en: It shows every detail of the scene, just like a photograph
It has to be drawn in bright colours to count as a diagram
It shows only the important things, with labels and arrows

quiz.why_en: Diagrams only show the things that are important; they have labels and arrows (p.54).

quiz.stem_en: Arun and Zara draw their prediction in one colour and their result in another. Why?

choices.en: So they can see easily whether the prediction was right

quiz.why_en: Using a different colour for the prediction makes the comparison clear (p.54).

quiz.stem_en: Players want to turn a wheelchair on a basketball court. What must they use?
quiz.why_en: Forces are needed to make things change direction (p.53, p.55).

quiz.stem_en: Your prediction turns out to be wrong. What is the best thing to say about that?

choices.en: The test was a waste of time

quiz.why_en: Sometimes, when a prediction is wrong you learn something new (p.55).

quiz.stem_en: Children run and turn each time someone shouts 'Change'. What are they changing?
quiz.why_en: Changing direction means turning to go a different way (p.53).

quiz.stem_en: Books are hung on a rubber band to stretch it, and its length is measured each time. Why is it a good idea to add just one book at a time?

choices.en: It makes the test finish faster
It makes the rubber band stronger
Only one thing changes, so the pattern is easy to see

quiz.why_en: Changing one thing at a time makes the measurements fair (p.46).

quiz.stem_en: You drop a clay ball from four different heights and watch how flat it becomes. Where should you write down what you found out?
quiz.why_en: Record your results by writing or drawing in a table (p.44).
